plan.topic: Plague status decoder, as of Oct 12, 2026: what's confirmed, reported and still unknown about the Irkutsk oblast lab worker's death
plan.angle: Open (as of Oct 12, 2026): 'On Oct 10, WHO said a key uncertainty remains the absence of a confirmed diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker' (WHO Disease Outbreak News). Then, credited and dated, in this order. Oct 6: WHO (Lindmeier), word for word: 'No cause of death has been officially confirmed to date and laboratory testing is reportedly underway.' Oct 8: Rospotrebnadzor 'rejected reports about a second person falling ill' (AP), and WHO asked about a reported second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause (Tedros). Oct 8–9: Irkutsk oblast governor Igor Kobzev reported about 5,000 lab tests with no dangerous pathogens and lifted restrictions; AP noted he did not explicitly say whether pneumonic plague had been ruled out. Oct 10: Russia's IHR focal point told WHO that no case of plague has been registered recently in Irkutsk Oblast and called the death 'pneumonia of undetermined etiology'; WHO said it has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission based on that information, and requested more lab and contact details. End on WHO still asking for confirmation of the diagnosis. Introduce her as 'a laboratory worker in Irkutsk oblast who died'. Close with 'If you have possible exposure and symptoms, contact a doctor or local health authority urgently' and 'If you're worried, talk to a health professional.' Title: 'Plague in Russia: What's Confirmed vs Suspected (as of Oct 12, 2026) #shorts'.

plan.why: WHO's Oct 10 'cause still unclear' statement is under 48 hours old, and the playbook names the dated decoder as the breaking-news Short format. The news angle stays in a Short and out of the long video. | fact-check: I verified a newer, primary source: WHO Disease Outbreak News DON620, 'Pneumonia of undetermined etiology - the Russian Federation', published Oct 10, 2026 (https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON620). The opening beat should credit this, not Reuters/CBC paraphrase. The DON says Russia's IHR National Focal Point told WHO 'no case of plague has been registered recently in Irkutsk Oblast', that there were no biosafety incidents, that contacts tested negative for high-threat pathogens, and that the death was 'pneumonia of undetermined etiology'. WHO: 'A key uncertainty remains the absence of a confirmed diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker.' WHO also says it 'has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission associated with this event' based on information from the NFP. AP (Oct 10) quotes a different WHO line: 'Additional clinical, epidemiological and laboratory information, including confirmation of the diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker, is required to improve confidence in the assessment.' Reports differ on test counts: the governor's figure was about 5,000, and AP on Oct 10 reported more than 5,500. Credit each figure to whoever said it and when, or drop the number. Every line must be credited to the body that said it, at its exact scope. The NFP's statement is Russia's claim relayed by WHO, not WHO's own finding. Never say 'ruled out' or 'not plague'. Re-check WHO, Rospotrebnadzor and CDC at publish time, because the DON may be updated. Keep 170 words or fewer: cut the Axios CDC line before cutting any dated WHO line.

package.title: Plague status as of Oct 12: what's confirmed vs suspected #shorts
package.description:
As of Oct 12, 2026: the plague diagnosis is still not confirmed. Oct 8: Rospotrebnadzor rejected reports of a second ill person (AP); Irkutsk oblast's governor said nearly 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens. Oct 10: WHO relays Russia's Oct 6 reply that "no case of plague has been registered recently in Irkutsk Oblast"; WHO says more testing, including confirmatory testing, may help establish the cause.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. If you're worried, talk to a health professional. Possible exposure plus fever, cough, shortness of breath or chest pain? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently.

Sources:
- WHO Disease Outbreak News, DON620: https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON620
- Associated Press (via Irish News), Oct 8: https://www.irishnews.com/news/world/russian-health-watchdog-denies-second-infection-in-suspected-plague-case-GPHI5D5QXZKP3JLISCSPKFTCS4/

script.hook_pattern: A plain search question with a dated answer credited to WHO (status decoder). The first frame shows the question with an 'AS OF OCT 12, 2026' pill. The answer ('not the diagnosis', WHO, Oct 10) comes within about 4 s. A dated timeline then runs in order. Each line is credited to the body that said it, on the day it said it. Where a report was published later than the statement it relays, both dates are shown (Oct 6 → Oct 10). The video ends on WHO saying more testing may help establish the cause, which loops back to 'what's confirmed?'.

factcheck.summary: This Short is accurate and safe, and it can publish once the minor fixes below are made. I checked every quote against the live sources: the WHO report (Disease Outbreak News 620, dated Oct 10, 2026), UN News for the Oct 6 Lindmeier quote, AP via Irish News (Oct 8), Al Jazeera (Oct 8), the Kyiv Independent (Oct 8; the governor posted on Telegram and Russian state media reported the quarantine lifted) and CDC's 'Signs and Symptoms of Plague' (updated May 15, 2024). All quotes match word for word. WHO's report confirms the 'key uncertainty' sentence, that Russia's Oct 6 reply contained 'no case of plague has been registered recently in Irkutsk Oblast' and 'pneumonia of undetermined etiology', that observation 'has been completed for all identified contacts', the line 'Based on the information provided by NFP, WHO has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission', and the sentence 'may assist in establishing the causative agent'. A search for statements from Oct 11–12 found nothing newer than WHO's Oct 10 report, so it is still the newest development. The piece is calm, every status line is dated and credited, it ends on the open question rather than the most reassuring line, and the safety lines are all there. The minor fixes: narration is about 174 words against the 170 target; one source title in the source list is wrong; the opening answer is unclear when spoken; and the on-screen 'CDC' tag sits on our own urgent-contact advice, which CDC doesn't say. Optional, if there's word budget: WHO's Van Kerkhove spoke on Oct 7 and isn't in the timeline. It adds nothing new beyond the Oct 6 and Oct 10 lines, so it's not required.

notes: Headline/stat frame (1.1s) is clean and reads fine.
At 5.1s the caption pill reads "10 —" and ends on a trailing em dash, a dangling fragment that is confusing if viewed out of context or paused.
Caption at 11.1s reads "WHO DIED —" and ends on a trailing dash — a dangling, slightly jarring fragment given the topic (a worker's death).
Caption at 18.9s reads "HAS BEEN OFFICIALLY" — ends on a dangling adverb, matching the known 'never end on a dangling word' problem pattern.
Caption at 25.3s ends on a comma: "ACCORDING TO AP,"
Caption at 29.2s is a dangling fragment: "ABOUT A SECOND" with no verb/object.
Automated audit flags a text/text overlap at 35.95s: the small "Lungs" label collides with the caption pill "WITH PNEUMONIA OF UNDETERMINED CAUSE."
The "Lungs" label itself is small and sits low on the torso, close to where the caption pill begins.
Caption at 45.6s ends on a comma: "AND THAT SAME DAY," — a dangling clause.
Second frame ("WAS LIFTED.") completes it, confirming the sentence is being split awkwardly across the shot.
Caption "WHO'S OCTOBER 10" is ambiguous — reads as "who is" rather than the WHO organization's report.

Second frame caption "HAS BEEN REGISTERED" doesn't obviously connect to the headline "Oct 10 WHO report / Relays Russia's Oct 6 reply"; it reads like it may belong to a different beat about case registration.
Caption "OF ALL IDENTIFIED" is a dangling fragment paired with the vague label "Undetermined etiology" — unclear what is being counted.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits at -13.5dB under voice, already in the target window, so only a tiny trim to 0.95 to keep it from creeping toward the loud edge; pause swells (i14/i15, whip at 24.2s) were under target so boosted toward -10dB, matching other transition swells. Fixed one spike (i28 bubble hit -3.8dB over speech) that was overpowering narration, cut it ~13dB. Thinned the two densest SFX clusters (the chip reveals at 61.8s and 85.2-87s) by dropping one redundant blip each to stay within the 3-4-per-second rule, and slightly pulled back the 'Cause undetermined' moment (i22) so that serious beat isn't SFX-crowded. Added two bespoke underscore moments for story weight without adding more stock hits.
